page|faq.title: FAQ
page|faq.content:
The short answers to what people ask most. Did not find yours — write to hello@brix22.coffee.

When do you roast?

Every Monday. The roast date is in every lot passport, and the product page shows the peak-flavour window: a week of degassing, then three weeks at its best.

Which grind should I choose?

The one you brew with: V60 and filter — medium-fine, espresso — fine, French press — coarse, cezve — the finest. If you own a grinder, take whole bean: ground coffee loses its aroma in a few days.

What is the °Bx on the bag?

The sugar content of the cherry at the moment of picking. A ripe coffee cherry gives 20–24 °Bx. We buy only what was picked inside that window — more about it here.

How long does coffee keep?

Whole bean holds its flavour for about six weeks from roasting, ground coffee for a few days. Keep it in a closed bag at room temperature, not in the fridge.

Do you sell gift certificates?

Yes, they will appear in the catalogue together with the tasting sets.

page|delivery.title: Delivery & payment
page|delivery.content:
We roast every Monday and ship the same day. Orders placed after Monday travel with the next batch.

Delivery

Nova Poshta — branch or parcel locker, 1–2 days. Free from 1,200 ₴; below that, at the carrier’s rates.

Pickup from the roastery at 41 Kyrylivska St — free, on weekdays from 9:00 to 18:00.

EU countries — Nova Poshta Global, 5–9 days, 450 ₴ per shipment regardless of weight. Any customs duty and taxes in the destination country are paid by the recipient.

Payment

Card online — Visa, Mastercard, Apple Pay and Google Pay. Card details are never stored on our server. Cash on delivery works inside Ukraine only — it is a Nova Poshta service; orders going abroad are paid by card.

Returns

If a lot did not suit you, write within a week and we will swap it for another at our cost. There is no need to send an opened bag back.

page|about.title: About us
page|about.content:
BRIX 22° is a roastery in Kyiv. We bring in microlots from farms we work with directly, and we put a passport in every bag: altitude, process, sugar content of the cherry at picking and the price the farmer received.

Why 22 degrees

Brix (°Bx) is a unit of sugar content in a liquid. The farmer measures the juice of the coffee cherry with a refractometer right on the tree: below 20 the cherry is unripe and the coffee comes out hollow, above 24 it is overripe. 22° is the middle of that window, the moment the cherry is worth picking.

What we do differently

Most roasters write “notes of berries and chocolate” and stop there. We sell data. Every figure in a lot passport was collected at the mill during picking and confirmed at purchase — and the same figure is on the bag, in the catalogue and on the transparency page.

We roast every Monday and ship the same day. We keep no warehouse of finished coffee: the bag that reaches you was roasted this week.

Honestly, about this demo

This is a concept project for a portfolio. The brand, the farm names, the SCA scores, the prices and the addresses are invented demo content.

product|guatemala-huehuetenango.title: Guatemala Huehuetenango
product|guatemala-huehuetenango.content: A natural process at altitude: dark berries, chocolate and a light spice. The body is dense, so this lot holds up well in a French press and a cezve.

meta.brix_lot_cup_notes: A natural process at altitude: dark berries, chocolate and a light spice. The body is dense, so this lot holds up well in a French press and a cezve.

product|rwanda-nyamasheke.title: Rwanda Nyamasheke
product|rwanda-nyamasheke.content: The honey process leaves the mucilage on the bean and gives honeyed sweetness without heaviness. The softest lot in the range — a good place to start if you are moving on from supermarket coffee.

product|kenya-nyeri-ab-lot-14.content: Double fermentation gives that very Kenyan blackcurrant. The acidity is bright and juicy, the body denser than in Ethiopian lots. It holds up to milk if you brew it stronger.

product|ethiopia-guji-hambela.title: Ethiopia Guji Hambela
product|ethiopia-guji-hambela.content: Eighteen days of dry fermentation on African beds give a dense berry sweetness. In a V60 it is ripe cherry and bergamot; as it cools, cocoa comes through. Milk mutes the acidity, so we suggest drinking this one black.

brix_farm|nyamasheke.title: Nyamasheke mill
brix_farm|nyamasheke.excerpt: A mill on the shore of Lake Kivu, working with the honey process since 2024.

meta.brix_farm_region_note: Western Rwanda, the shores of Lake Kivu. Altitude and cool nights stretch out the ripening.
meta.brix_farm_story: The mill moved to the honey process in 2024: the mucilage is left on the bean and dried slowly. That takes constant turning, but it gives the honeyed sweetness the local washed lots do not have.
meta.brix_farm_quote: Honey is harder here than washed. But it shows that our hills can do more.
meta.brix_farm_year_calendar_1_brix_farm_cale: Cherry from 20 °Bx, the rest kept apart

brix_farm|el-paraiso.title: El Paraíso farm
brix_farm|el-paraiso.excerpt: A family farm in Huila that specialises in controlled fermentations.

meta.brix_farm_headline: Fermentation as a recipe, not an accident
meta.brix_farm_region_note: The department of Huila, the slopes of the Central Andes. Two harvests a year.
meta.brix_farm_story: Diego runs fermentation in closed tanks with temperature and pH control, records every batch and repeats the successful protocols the following season. It is closer to winemaking than to the usual coffee processing.
meta.brix_farm_quote: I am not after a wild flavour. I am after the same flavour in the next harvest.

brix_farm|gathaithi.title: Gathaithi factory
brix_farm|gathaithi.excerpt: The wet mill of the Tegu cooperative in Nyeri county.

meta.brix_farm_region_note: Central Kenya, the slopes of Nyeri. Red volcanic soil and two picking campaigns a year.
meta.brix_farm_story: Gathaithi is one of the four factories of the Tegu cooperative. Cherry is taken in daily until eight in the evening, sorted in water and fermented twice with a wash in between.
meta.brix_farm_quote: Double fermentation costs a day. But it is what gives the blackcurrant people come back to us for.
meta.brix_farm_year_calendar_0_brix_farm_cale: The main harvest is set here

brix_farm|kebele-12.title: Kebele 12 station
brix_farm|kebele-12.excerpt: A collection station in the Guji zone working with 640 smallholders.

meta.brix_farm_region_note: Southern Ethiopia, the Guji zone. The dry season runs from December to March — exactly when the cherry is dried on open-air beds.
meta.brix_farm_story:
Kebele 12 takes cherry from smallholders within a seven-kilometre radius. The average plot is under a hectare, so the quality of a lot depends not on one farm but on how the station sorts and dries what is brought to it.

We first came here in 2023 with the importer we work with. The station was already measuring °Bx, but only on a sample basis. We agreed on something simple: we pay a premium for batches picked from 20 °Bx, and we buy them separately from the rest of the harvest.
meta.brix_farm_quote: Selective picking costs more on every kilo. It only makes sense when the buyer pays for it separately.

brix_guide|turka.title: Cezve
brix_guide|turka.excerpt: The finest grind and no boiling: a dense cup the eastern way.

meta.brix_guide_tip_text: The moment the foam starts to rise, take it off the heat. Boiling takes the aroma away.
meta.brix_guide_steps_0_brix_guide_step_text: Add the coffee and pour in cold water.
meta.brix_guide_steps_1_brix_guide_step_text: Do not stir once it starts heating.
meta.brix_guide_steps_2_brix_guide_step_text: Let it settle and repeat once more.

brix_guide|french-press.title: French press
brix_guide|french-press.excerpt: The simplest method: a dense body and full flavour with no equipment.

meta.brix_guide_tip_title: Do not push the plunger to the bottom
meta.brix_guide_tip_text: Lower it only to the surface and pour — the grounds stay below and the cup is cleaner.
meta.brix_guide_steps_0_brix_guide_step_text: Pour the water in and stir.
meta.brix_guide_steps_1_brix_guide_step_text: Skim the foam off the top with two spoons.
meta.brix_guide_steps_2_brix_guide_step_text: Lower the plunger to the surface and pour.

brix_guide|espresso.title: Espresso
brix_guide|espresso.excerpt: 18 g into 40 g in 28 seconds — the starting point for dialling in the grind.

meta.brix_guide_tip_title: If it runs faster than 24 seconds
meta.brix_guide_tip_text: Make the grind one step finer. If it is slower than 34 — one step coarser instead.
meta.brix_guide_steps_0_brix_guide_step_text: Level it out and press with steady force.
meta.brix_guide_steps_1_brix_guide_step_text: If your machine can, let the coffee swell.
meta.brix_guide_steps_2_brix_guide_step_text: Weigh the result rather than watching the volume.

brix_guide|aeropress.title: Aeropress
brix_guide|aeropress.excerpt: A quick recipe for travelling: a denser body, less acidity.

meta.brix_guide_tip_text: If you want a longer extraction, brew it inverted and flip it 20 seconds before pressing.
meta.brix_guide_steps_0_brix_guide_step_text: Pour the water in at once and stir twice.
meta.brix_guide_steps_1_brix_guide_step_text: Cover with the filter and let it stand.
meta.brix_guide_steps_2_brix_guide_step_text: Press evenly, without force. Stop at the hiss.

brix_guide|v60.title: V60
brix_guide|v60.excerpt: The classic recipe for a Hario V60: a clean cup, pronounced acidity.

meta.brix_guide_tip_text: Boil the water and wait 45 seconds with the lid open — that gives about 93 °C.
meta.brix_guide_steps_0_brix_guide_step_text: Pour in 45 g of water, stir with a spoon and let the coffee open up.
meta.brix_guide_steps_1_brix_guide_step_text: Pour in a slow spiral from the centre outwards.
meta.brix_guide_steps_2_brix_guide_step_text: Do not pour onto the walls of the dripper.
meta.brix_guide_steps_3_brix_guide_step_text: The water should pass through completely. The bed is flat, with no craters.

page|privacy.title: Privacy policy
page|privacy.content:
Briefly and without legal fog: what data we ask for, why, and who gets to see it.

Who we are

BRIX 22° is a specialty coffee roastery at 41 Kyrylivska St, Kyiv. Anything about your data goes to hello@brix22.coffee.

What we collect

For an order: your name, phone, email and delivery address or Nova Poshta branch. For an account: also a password (we store only its hash), your order history and BRIX Club subscription. From the café form: the venue name and contacts.

Why

To roast, ship and follow up on your order: send the confirmation, the tracking number and status updates. The Monday letter goes only to those who subscribed, and every letter has an unsubscribe link.

Who we share it with

Nova Poshta — name, phone and address, without which the parcel cannot be delivered. LiqPay — the amount and order number. You enter your card details on LiqPay’s page, and they never reach us. Nobody else, and we sell nothing.

Cookies

The cart and checkout rely on a session cookie — without it the site would not remember what you put in the cart. Another cookie remembers your chosen currency. WooCommerce records where you came to the site from, so we can see which advertising works. If Google Analytics is enabled, it receives anonymised page-view data.

How long we keep it

Orders — as long as accounting requires. Your account — until you delete it.

Your rights

You can view and correct your data in your account. To get a copy or have it erased, write to hello@brix22.coffee — we reply within 30 days.
